newsitem.title: USA: US spring wheat tour sees below average yields.
newsitem.headline: US spring wheat tour sees below average yields.

text.p: The 1997 U.S. spring wheat crop tour ended on Thursday with participants calculating an average dark northern spring (DNS) wheat yield potential of 31.3 bushels per acre (bpa), down from the 36.4 bpa in last year's tour.
The tour also calculated an average durum wheat yield potential of 27.7 bpa, against 29.7 bushels in last year's tour.

The 55 tour participants, representing a cross-section of the grain industry, spent three days inspecting wheat fields in North Dakota and Minnesota, two top producing states. The tour is organized annually by the Wheat Quality Council.

In its July crop report released earlier this month, the U.S. Agriculture Department estimated this year's DNS wheat production in North Dakota, historically the top U.S. spring wheat state, at 212.5 million bushels at an average yield 25.0 bushels per acre.
Last year, North Dakota produced 313.5 million bu at an average yield of 33.0 bpa. The five-year average yield is 32.5 bpa.
North Dakota harvested 79.38 million bushels of durum in 1996, at an average yield of 27.0 bpa. The five year average durum yield in the state is 31.9 bpa.

Tour members said the below-average yields were partly a result of an early-summer drought that caused erratic plant emergence, weed and disease pressure. Participants also said the crop in the Red River Valley region was suffering from scab, a fungus that can reduce wheat yields.
